April 2009 ## Into the depths of recession… - Preliminary data for the first quarter of 2009 indicates that global demand for copper and copper alloy mill products fell for the fourth successive quarter on a year-onyear basis, and for the third successive quarter on a sequential basis. The speed of decline accelerated in Q1 2009 with a provisional 22% year-on-year contraction, following on from a deep 15% slump in Q4 2008. The recession has now become near universal with almost every product line, end use market and region affected. - The flat rolled products business continues to experience the deepest slump in offtake due to acute destocking by consumers and end users. Copper plate, sheet, strip and foil consumption slumped 32% year-on-year in Q1 2009, while shipments of alloy products plunged 25% compared to year-ago levels. Copper tube demand dropped 18% and alloy rod fell 22%. Japan and Taiwan have seen the deepest declines, though there is some hope that the worst may now be past in South Korea and China, although the performance by product line and end use is still very patchy. |Consumptio

2009 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 2 of 12 **April 2009** Copper and copper alloy mill products www.crumonitor.com # Plate, sheet, strip and foil ### Japanese production in severe decline **Japanese** output of rolled copper products dived by almost 60% y-o-y in February, the seventh straight month of decline. Market participants cannot tell whether the market has reached bottom. Poor domestic vehicle sales, the lowest in 32 years, have impacted copper semis makers. **Kobe Steel Ltd.** is likely to announce its first group loss in seven years; its copper sheet plant in **Yamaguchi Prefecture** is operating at low rate. **Furukawa Electric Co., Ltd.** decreased copper foil production in Q1 by 70-80% compared to earlier plans. The company shut down operations at **Imaichi** and **Imaichi-Higashi** for three days in March. Responding to lower demand, copper foil makers have cut copper scrap procurement by 10-30% compared to usual levels. In copper sheet, Japan‟s **Fair Trade Commission** ordered four companies to stop advertising that their copper strip products strengthen cell phone signal reception. ### Chinese growth is hit but some glimmer of hope is evident The global economic slowdown has taken its toll on the aggressively expanding **Chinese** copper market. Due to plunging copper plate and strip demand, **Anhui Jingcheng Copper Share Co., Ltd.** reported a net loss of RMB 42.7 million (US$6.2 million) in 2008. The company is planning to produce 73,000 tonnes of copper plate and strip in 2009, down by 20,000 tonnes compared to previous plans. As part of a non-ferrous metals stimulus plan, the **State Administration of Taxation** increased its export tax rebates from April 1st . As a result, copper plate‟s export tax rebate rose to 9% and that of copper foil to 13%. Additional governmental support refers to copper semis projects announced in **Henan Province** , with two high precision copper sheet and coil projects to receive funding. First, the project of **Chalco Luoyang Copper Co., Ltd.** will have a capacity of 100,000 tpy while the project of **Henan Sanfeng Copper Co., Ltd.** will have a capacity of 50,000 tpy. Industrial expansion generates some optimism for the future. ### The Western Word: low demand and credit unavailability Market participants reported a 20-30%

y-o-y business contraction in Q1. In the **US** , industrial production has been seriously hit. In **Germany** , **Wieland-Werke** is introducing short-time working for 3,450 staff. In **Italy** , **KME Group** announced that its 2008 total output fell by 8.6% y-o-y to 571,000 t. Market visibility remains low and due to the uncertainty market forecasting is impossible. ### End-use segments: automotive and electronics sectors Vehicle sales in the **US** plunged by 38% y-o-y in Q1. In the first two months of the year, **North American** vehicle production plummeted by 58% y-o-y. Top seller premium auto maker **BMW** saw its global sales shrinking by 21% y-o-y in Q1. **Mercedes-Benz** global car sales fell by 25% y-o-y in the same period. In the **UK** , new car registrations declined by 30% y-o-y in Q1. Car sales are anticipated to remain strong in **China** , which in January surpassed the **US** to become the world‟s largest auto market. **India** is expected to bounce back quickly, supported by low-cost car launches. However, the global car and truck market may take more than a decade to reach its 2007 peak levels. According to the **China Semiconductor Industry Association** , the local integrated circuit industry is beginning to slow. Data released by the **US Semiconductor Industry Association** showed that global sales of computer chips plunged by 30% y-o-y in February. The Copper and Brass Servicenter Association reported US copper tube imports in the first two months of 2009 contracted by 14% y-o-y. An economist from the **Associated General Contractors of America** told CRU that there is almost no demand for commercial construction. This is having an adverse effect on both copper plumbing and air conditioning tube consumption. However, construction firms have recently become keener and project bids are coming in much lower than expected. During the 8th World Copper Conference at Santiago, a leading US tube manufacturer said that the US market in January and February was grim but was beginning to improve sequentially in March. The improvement will mainly come from the construction sector while restocking activity is expected in the coming months. Meanwhile, **Wolverine Tube** extended the expiration date of the previously announced exchange offer and consent solicitation to 14th April, 2009. Chilean copper tube manufacturer **Madeco** said that it decided to focus its core business on making plastic resealable freezer bags. The company said it is difficult for them to predict price movements and all of their clients associated with the construction market in Chile and Argentina are suffering. ### Chinese tube demand remains weak in Q1 Copper tube production in Asia declined by 17.4% y-o-y to 285,000 tonnes in Q1. Our Beijing analyst reported that tube demand in China has been very weak starting from April last year. CRU understands that the business of **Golden Dragon** , the leading commercial tube producer in China, had worsened by at least 20% compared to last year. Industry participants think that the government‟s stimulus package will not have a significant impact for at least the next six months. The recent tax rebates increase was not helpful because it will not improve overseas consumption. According to our data, Chinese exports in Q1 declined by 29% y-o-y to 35,000 tonnes from 49,700 tonnes in Q1 2008. CRU h

as also heard that a number of small tube manufacturing plants in China have closed down and there have been some job cuts in the industry. Although the industry‟s general consensus is pessimistic, the Chinese construction sector has a better outlook, which would eventually support tube demand and air conditioner sales. In Japan, **Kobelco & Materials** revised its net sales forecast down by ¥30 billion to ¥2,170 billion (US$21.7 billion) due to lower sales volume in a number of segments including copper products. Consolidated operating income is forecast to decline by ¥8 billion to ¥111 billion (US$1.11 billion) compared to the previous forecast as a result. **Sumitomo Light Metal Industries** announced in March that it expected to slash copper tube output by 30% in Q1 compared to Q1 2008 by shutting down operations at **Copper Works** in Toyokawa city. The company said that the decision was based on lower demand due to the global recession and particularly to the downturn in the air conditioner industry. Positive signs from European construction market CRU believes that European tube consumption may be able to stabilise in the coming months, given that there are signs of improvement in demand from the construction sector and Q1 copper tube imports increased y-o-y in Greece, the Nordic and Benelux regions. Markit reported that manufacturing production indices for European private sector economy were showing a slower contraction in March. The production index for the construction and materials segment in March increased by 5.2% to about 33 (any number below 50 indicates a contraction), which is a good sign as 100% of copper plumbing tube is consumed by the construction sector. **KME** , the Italian semis producer, confirmed that among the range of copper products, copper plumbing tube is suffering less than others mainly due to the fact that the copper price has come down to a reasonable level. CRU now estimates that world consumption contracted by 15% year-on-year in Q4 2008, resulting in a 6.2% decrease in world offtake to 2.9 million tonnes last year. More disturbingly, the rate of decline appears to have accelerated through the first quarter of 2009 with a 22% year-on-year decline likely in Q1 2009 according to our preliminary data. This would be the fourth consecutive sequential decline in demand since Q1 2008, when consumption reached 791,000 tonnes, compared to our estimate of 613,000 tonnes for the opening quarter of 2009. Moreover, if industrial activity continues at this slack pace, then world output will certainly fall well short of the 2001 recessionary low of 2.7 million tonnes. ### Regionally…bad or worse…almost everywhere There is little good news to be found in any of the major regi

onal markets.  In Europe, Italian brass rod output dropped 22% year-on-year in Q4 2008, and we expect that will have deteriorated by closer to 30% in Q1 2009, compared to the strongest quarter of 2008.  Many German mills are also now on short time working patterns to adjust to the acute destocking programs enacted by consumers in response to the “ _exceptional and unforeseen_ ” slowdown in the marketplace.  Order inflows are significantly below yearago levels across almost every end use market segment, but with construction products and automotive particularly harshly affected.  In North America, the situation is at least as bad, if not worse.  US output of alloy rod and wire plunged 44% year-on-year in December and by 42% year-on-year in January, although at least January‟s production of 16,273mt was sequentially higher than the 12,760mt in December. However, early indications suggest that output and demand were no better in February than January. 

### Japanese market in freefall as users de-stock 

Japanese consumption of alloy rod and bar has collapsed following a severe and prolonged destocking program by consumers and wholesalers in the run up to the end of the Japanese fiscal year.  Industry output dropped 34.4% from year-ago levels in January, followed by a 45.7% slump in February and a projected 49.0% decline in March to less than 10,000 tonnes per month.  Mills are planning to take a record number of “temporary closing days” in April amid signs that the market has yet to hit bottom, as consumers are showing no indications of restocking despite the recent rise in brass scrap prices.  Yet amid the current market turmoil **Nippon Shindo** has confirmed that it is proceeding with its plan to begin construction of its new brass bar and alloy wire plant in Sakai City, Osaka, starting from August.  It will invest ¥12 billion (US$121m) on the 36,700 sqm site and install two 1,000kW horizontal continuous casting furnaces and two 450kW vertical casting furnaces and a 3,000 tonne indirect extrusion press to process longer billets with higher yields.  Commercial production is scheduled to start in December 2010. 

### Taiwan / China / South Korea is more of a mixed picture 

Taiwanese demand appears to be as depressed as Japan, with January‟s production volume down 48.5% year-on-year to little more than 5,000 tonnes per month compared to more than 10,000 tonnes per month typically.  However, mill inventories have been well managed enabling any future recovery in demand to be quickly translated into increased output.  In Mainland China, there are tentative signs that the worst may now be over, with Chinese buying interest emerging strongly for all grades of brass scrap.  But dealers and exporters are no longer so eager to do business with China given fears of payment defaults and contract reneging living so recently in the memory. **www.crumonitor.com** # **Copper** Raw Materials trends Throughout February copper was trading between US$3,2003,400 per tonne. It was a month characterised by price stability. During that period, LME stocks were rising, peaking at 548,400 tonnes on February 24th . March saw significant gains in prices along with reduction in stocks, which was supported by the Chinese SRB purchases and unavailability of copper scrap. A favourable LME/SHFE differential triggered shipments from Europe to China. LME cancelled warrants soared after mid-February and during March. As a result, LME stocks fell to 500,000 tonnes in early April. From the fundamentals point of view, demand remains particularly weak and supply has responded only partially. Despite the current rally, which was quite aggressive in late March-early April, price expectations are bearish since end-use demand remains particularly sluggish due to the ongoing economic slowdown. According to a joint statement of the two organisations, it was the first time that about 60,000 salmon were harvested in copper cages. The programme was part of a broader plan of the two organisations which looks for new potential applications for copper usage. Codelco said that the use of copper benefits salmon farming because of its antimicrobial properties. The outcome of the research showed that there was a decrease in salmon mortality and better oxygenation in specimens. - According to a survey conducted by the state nonferrous metals association **Sindi

cel** in **Sao Paulo** , shipments of 35% of copper semis producers in **Brazil** are expected to fall by at least 10% y-o-y in 2009.  The same survey showed that 18% of manufacturers anticipate up to a 10% sales contraction and 12% expect business to remain at the same level.  As a result of the credit squeeze and weak demand, 59% reported a 10% y-o-y plunge in February‟s net revenues.  Sindicel said that the ongoing price competition in the market and the high taxes imposed by the Brazilian government have affected industrial competitiveness, especially export performance. 

- The latest survey statistics from the **Copper and Brass Servicenter Association (CBSA)** reported that February 2009 total US copper and alloy shipments declined at the fastest rate ever since the survey began 40 years ago, down by 20% from January 2009 and 35% from February 2008.  The data indicates that copper sheet shipments plummeted by 47.1% y-o-y to 1,473t in February. Copper rod shipments also declined by 33.5% y-o-y to 1,674t for the same month.  Copper pipe and plate shipments both fell slightly by 4.5% y-o-y and 4.1% y-o-y respectively.  Total copper and alloy product shipments fell by 40.6% y-o-y to 8,573t in February. 

- **Standard & Poor** has announced that it placed credit ratings for **Wolverine Tube Inc.** on CreditWatch.  The decision includes its „CC‟ corporate rating and „C‟ senior unsecured debt. Wolverine Tube announced its decision to extend the expiration data of an exchange offer of senior notes due 2009 for new ones due 2012. 

- **Wieland-Werke** announced that because of a major decline in customer orders, it will implement short-time working for 3,450 staff.  The company attributed its decision to lower activity in all geographical segments and product categories caused by the global slowdown.  As a result, weakening business particularly in the automobile, electronics and construction sectors have affected the company.  Impacted staff of Wieland-Werke will work 20% less than normal. 

- **Jiangxi Copper Co.** reported operating revenue of RMB 53.9 billion in 2008, an increase of 24.5% compared with 2007.  Net profit declined 49.6% y-o-y to RMB 2.3 billion.  The company expanded copper processing capacity for tubes, foils and enamelled wire over 2008 to 480,000 tonnes per year from 370,000 tonnes per year and has plans to produce 480,000 tonnes of copper rod, wire and other products in 2009. 

- **Chinalco Luoyang Copper Co., Ltd** . is working on a 100ktpy high-precision copper plate, sheet and strip project.  According to a survey carried out by **Antaike** , the project is expected to start operations at the end of 2009. Upon completion of the project, the company will have 200ktpy of copper plate, sheet and strip output capacity. In 2008 Luoyang Copper produced 70,000 tonnes of copper plate, sheet and strip, and 20,000 tonnes of copper tube and copper wirerod. 

- With a view to supporting growth, the **State Administration of Taxation**

in **China** increased its export tax rebates on copper foil, plate and tube with effect from 1<sup>st</sup> April.  The policy was announced on 27<sup>th</sup> March and is aimed at boosting Chinese exports.  Copper plate‟s export tax rebate rose from 5% to 9%, copper foil‟s from 5% to 13%, and copper tube‟s from 9% to 13%.  It is expected that by providing extra export stimulus the measure will support copper semis production.

2003.  LME copper prices jumped to US$4,330/t on April 6th, an increase of 41% compared with the beginning of the year.  Lately, copper prices have been supported by optimism generated by the Chinese and the US government spending packages.  The new infrastructure projects in China will boost the demand for copper semis, especially tubes and cables. 









- **Sumitomo Light Metal Industries Ltd.** is expecting to cut its domestic copper tube output by 30% in Q1 2009 compared to the same period in 2008 and its original plans.  The decision is attributed to the ongoing global economic recession and particularly to the downturn experienced in the air conditioning industry.  As a result, the company is shutting down operations for two days a month at Copper Works in **Toyokawa City, Aichi** . 

- According to data released by the **Japan Copper and Brass Association** , production of rolled copper products in February plunged by 58.5% y-o-y to 37,381 tonnes on a seasonally adjusted basis.  This decline was the seventh consecutive monthly decrease and the largest ever recorded.  On an unadjusted basis it was the biggest decline in 34 years.  When compared with January, output plummeted by 18.7%.  As a result of weak demand for copper semis, Japanese smelter production has fallen by 10% y-o-y since the beginning of the year. 

- **Tongling Nonferrous Metals Group Co., Ltd.** has recently introduced lead-free easy-cutting bar products.  This kind of bar product is widely used in home appliances manufacturing.  Examples include air conditioners, heat exchangers and telescopic antennas.  The company is also holding a bid for a 275ktpy high precision copper and copper alloy bar production line.  The project includes 20ktpy of red copper and profile, 220ktpy of brass bar and 45ktpy of copper alloy profile. 

- A new energy-efficient standard is expected to be introduced by home air conditioner makers in **China** .  By making the condenser and evaporator bigger, an energy-efficiency ratio of 3.0 can be achieved, compared to the current ratio of 2.6.  In the past, these two parts were entirely made of copper.  However, due to the wide copper-aluminium differential, there has been

a tendency in the industry to replace copper with aluminium.
